See also: jeù and je'u

Translingual

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Abbreviation of English Jonkor Bourmataguil with e as a placeholder, influenced by Dougne.

Symbol

[edit]

jeu

  1. (international standards) ISO 639-3 language code for Jonkor Bourmataguil.

See also

[edit]
  • Wiktionary’s coverage of Jonkor Bourmataguil terms

Catalan

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈʒɛw]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈd͡ʒɛw]

Verb

[edit]

jeu

  1. inflection of jeure:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative
  2. inflection of jaure:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French geu, gieu, giu, from Latin iocus, jocus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ʒø/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

jeu m (plural jeux)

  1. game (activity performed for amusement)
  2. play (in a theatre/theater)
  3. set (of objects that belong together)
  4. manner of handling a gun
  5. play (mechanics: a space between two adjacent parts to allow free movement)
  6. a pipe organ stop
  7. a hand of playing cards
